main_body: Wooden lectern/pulpit box (x7-39, rows 12-45) with an orange lid slab, a dark-framed red book panel with a gold cross on the front, and a dark plinth. The staircase on the right is a secondary part.
top_band: Orange lid band at rows ~12-15 (about 4 rows, lightest wood tone), then a darker brown row at 16 before the front face
evidence: Down the middle column: red cushion and book on top, orange lid band (rows 12-15), a dark brown eave row (16), then the front face (rows 17-41) with an inset dark frame around the red panel, then the plinth (42-45). The lid is only about 4 rows, with no distinct bright front-edge line, so it is marginal, but the eave shadow and inset panel keep it readable as a 3/4 piece.

style.evidence: The outlines are dark brown, tinted to match the wood, which is good. The red book panel is a large flat fill of about 14x14 px with only a gold cross and a one-column highlight. The wood sides, plinth and stair risers are also flat bands with no grain or speckle. The material ramps have only about 3-4 steps, and most tiles use 3-5 colours. Next to the stall and well references (tile scallops, stone-by-stone shading, grain) it looks flatter and thinner.
